name: security
description: Security SkillPack: secret-leak detection plus dangerous-command guard. Two phases — secret vocabulary and dynamic-exec vocabulary — combined in one HandManifest.

phases.name: secret-leak-vocabulary
phases.body: Phase 1 — secret-leak detection. Reuse SecretDetector's named patterns (sk-ant-, sk-proj-, AKIA-prefixed AWS access keys, ya29.* GCP OAuth, sk_(live|test) Stripe, gh[pousr]_ GitHub, hf_ HuggingFace, npm_, AC-prefixed Twilio SIDs, generic api_key=/auth_token=/bearer literals) as the vocabulary. Never paste these literals into source files; never include them in chat history; never echo them to logs. When you encounter a value that looks like one of these patterns, redact it before writing it anywhere. The credential vault (`senkani vault add`) is the storage path; environment variables injected via the credential gateway are the runtime path.

phases.name: dangerous-command-vocabulary
phases.body: Phase 2 — dangerous-command guard. Refuse to introduce or execute dynamic-evaluation vectors: `eval()` of untrusted input (Python/JS/Ruby), `exec()` against unsanitized arguments, dynamic SQL built by string concatenation, and shell pipes that interpolate user input directly. Prefer parameterized SQL, prepared statements, and explicit argv arrays. When asked to run a Bash command that contains shell-injection patterns (unquoted variable in a path argument, backticks, $(...) inside a single-quoted string), pause and rewrite the command into a safer form before executing.

skill_md:
# security

Secret-leak detection + dangerous-command guard, combined.

Use this skill when authoring code that handles credentials, when reviewing diffs, and when running shell commands that touch sensitive paths. The secret-leak phase reuses SecretDetector's vocabulary to keep the rule set consistent with the rest of Senkani's pipeline; the dangerous-command phase blocks the most common dynamic-eval and injection vectors.

The paired HookRouter policy fragment denies hard-coded API_KEY assignments, hard-coded password literals, and `eval(` invocations at the tool boundary. Override is `senkani pack uninstall security`. Read-only operations on existing secrets (e.g. `senkani vault list`) are unaffected.
